concepts.title: Resist methods: clay pastes, lime outlines and wax
concepts.summary: Ajrakh gach is a paste of tree gum, clay (lal mitti), water and millet flour, with alum added to half of it; the clay and millet resist indigo while the alum acts as mordant.
concepts.body_md:
Ajrakh gach is a paste of tree gum, clay (lal mitti), water and millet flour, with alum added to half of it; the clay and millet resist indigo while the alum acts as mordant. [ajrakh:S1]

Ajrakh white outlines (khariyanu) are printed with a lime and tree-gum resist. [ajrakh:S1]

Dabu paste is mud, gum and lime; the Deesa paste uses river-bed silt. [dabu:S1, dabu:S3]

An Akola account lists three mud resists: chuna (lime) or kirana, the weakest, for fine outlines; mitti (mud) when the cloth is immersed in indigo a few times; and rait (sand), the strongest, for the most absorbent colours. [dabu:S6]

Bagru and Sanganeri dabu paste is prepared by mixing kali mitti (clay soil), lime, wheat flour and gum in specific ratios depending on the type of dabu paste needed, and the technique is used only for creating patterns with indigo blue. [bagru:S1, sanganeri:S1]

Beeswax is listed among the Machilipatnam Kalamkari raw materials; an Asia InCH account of Machilipatnam describes a wax resist hand-printed with a kalam before the indigo is applied. [machilipatnam-kalamkari:S4, machilipatnam-kalamkari:S5]
